items.title: Researchers outline limits of measuring online religious hostility from a bounded sample
items.summary: A methods briefing stresses that a monitored comment sample cannot stand in for a whole platform, and that a news event may coincide with a change without explaining it.

items.title: Police in several English forces publish mid-year religious-hate incident figures
items.summary: Forces released recorded-incident counts for the first half of the year. Officials said the tables are police records, not a measure of all harm, and urged people to keep reporting.

items.title: High court to hear planning challenge over a proposed Islamic centre
items.summary: Campaigners and the local authority disagree over traffic and heritage grounds. The listing is a planning dispute, not a finding about the congregation.

items.title: Statistics Canada to publish updated police-reported hate-crime tables
items.summary: The agency said the next release will include religion as a motivation category. Analysts cautioned that changes in reporting practice can move the totals without a change in incidents.

items.title: Senate hearing on campus religious liberty draws competing testimony
items.summary: Witnesses disagreed over speech codes and security after spring protests. The record is testimony, not a determination that any group caused later online activity.

items.title: Canadian cities add transit and public-square space for Eid gatherings
items.summary: Municipal statements described extra buses and stewarding. Coverage is of civic logistics around a religious holiday, not of online classifications.

items.title: Why a protest and a comment spike can sit in the same week without one proving the other
items.summary: An explainer walks through temporal association, collection gaps, and the risk of reading a news headline as a cause of later posts.

items.title: Ontario school board reviews religious-holiday policy after parent complaints
items.summary: Trustees asked staff for a paper on exam dates and excused absences. The story is a local education-policy debate.

items.title: Embassy protest in London remains peaceful, organisers and police say
items.summary: A Saturday march stayed on the authorised route. Police reported no arrests at the time of writing. The article does not assess later online commentary.

items.title: Commons hears questions on mosque safety after vandalism in a northern city
items.summary: MPs asked about patrols and repair funding after windows were broken at a mosque overnight. Police said the investigation was open and asked the public not to speculate about motive.

items.title: Justice Department files brief in a workplace religious-accommodation case
items.summary: The brief argues how existing statute should apply to schedule changes. It is a court filing, not a statement about online hate or about any monitored sample.

items.title: Federal briefing notes upcoming consultation on online-harm reporting forms
items.summary: Officials said the consultation will ask civil-society groups how incident forms should record religion as a target category. No draft regulation was published with the note.
